biomarkers.name: KRAS
biomarkers.clinical_use: Predicts lack of benefit from anti-EGFR therapy in RAS-mutant disease

biomarkers.name: GNAS
biomarkers.clinical_use: Enriched in mucinous appendiceal neoplasms and adenocarcinomas; useful diagnostically

biomarkers.name: TP53
biomarkers.prevalence: ~20-40% (more frequent in high-grade and non-mucinous tumors)
biomarkers.clinical_use: More common in aggressive non-mucinous / high-grade subtypes

biomarkers.name: MSI / dMMR
biomarkers.clinical_use: Predicts benefit from immune checkpoint inhibitors if MSI-H/dMMR

biomarkers.name: BRAF V600E
biomarkers.clinical_use: If present, may support use of BRAF-targeted therapy regimens extrapolated from colorectal cancer

biomarkers.name: HER2
biomarkers.clinical_use: Trastuzumab-based therapy may be considered if amplified/overexpressed

biomarkers.name: CEA, CA 19-9, CA 125
biomarkers.clinical_use: Used for disease monitoring; CA 19-9 and CA-125 are often informative in mucinous / peritoneal disease

biomarkers.name: RNF43
biomarkers.clinical_use: Recurrently altered in appendiceal mucinous neoplasia/adenocarcinoma; currently mainly of molecular characterization interest

biomarkers.name: NRAS
biomarkers.clinical_use: As a RAS alteration, predicts lack of benefit from anti-EGFR therapy

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Adenocarcinoma of appendiceal mucosa; often mucin-producing
histomorphological_subtype.grading: PSOGI/WHO grading incorporates cellularity, atypia, mitoses, and signet ring cell component; grading is especially important for mucinous peritoneal disease

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Poorly characterised; peritoneal spread pattern dominates
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Extensive extracellular mucin production; peritoneal implants are often paucicellular in low-grade mucinous disease

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Appendiceal mucosal epithelium (goblet cell adenocarcinoma may arise from crypt base progenitor cells with mixed neuroendocrine features)
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Colonic-type adenocarcinoma resembles conventional colorectal adenocarcinoma; goblet cell adenocarcinoma has mixed glandular + neuroendocrine differentiation
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Goblet cell adenocarcinoma represents a mixed lineage phenotype — a biphenotypic progenitor has been proposed to explain concurrent glandular and neuroendocrine differentiation
